## Why this unit matters

Move remote-call mechanics out of Order business logic. Study Feign's declarative contract, then design deadlines, logging, compression and retry policies.

The same shop remains the anchor: Product owns catalogue information, User owns customer information, and Order coordinates checkout. Read each chapter in order to see which new requirement motivates the next design decision.

## Lessons

1. **[Feign: Declarative HTTP Calls](feign-basics.qmd)**
2. **[Feign Configuration and Internals](feign-configuration.qmd)**

## Learning objective

After this unit, describe the dependency or operational problem **before** naming a framework; draw the relevant call/event path; state the failure mode and trade-off; and explain how the concept applies to a small TypeScript or NestJS service.

**Supplied source:** Day 2 §1–3. The content is an original explanation of the supplied course's topics and not a reproduction of its Java code. ## Mathematical Abstraction

A remote client maps a typed operation into an HTTP invocation.

$$
f:(\mathrm{method},\mathrm{arguments})\mapsto(\mathrm{request},\mathrm{response\ or\ error})
$$

$f$ represents a protocol adapter, not a local computation guaranteed to terminate.
